title: CT radiomics and deep learning predict survival after liposarcoma resection
summary: In 367 patients from two institutions, a model combining a radiomics signature, a ResNet-101 deep learning signature trained with Cox loss and clinicopathologic variables (RDCS) achieved C-indices of 0.775 in training, 0.704 internal and 0.725 in an external test cohort of 184 patients. In an exploratory external subset (n=82), C-index was 0.746 against 0.590 for the Sarculator application. The study is retrospective and in a rare tumor.
ai_technology: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-101 with Cox partial-likelihood loss plus radiomics

evidence.tested: Training and internal validation (institution 1) and external test cohort (institution 2, n=184).
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; rare tumor; needs prospective validation; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning signature from CT contributes to the survival prediction model.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Author affiliations and publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
